content:
Let \(\alpha=\angle BAC\), \(\beta=\angle ABC\), \(\gamma=\angle ACB\).

Since \(ABC\) is acute, \(O\) lies inside the triangle. Also \(X\), the intersection of two interior cevians, lies inside, so \(O\) and \(X\) are on the same side of \(BC\). Thus in the circle through \(B,O,X,C\), the angles subtending chord \(BC\) are equal:
\[
\angle BOC=\angle BXC.
\]
Because \(O\) is the circumcenter,
\[
\angle BOC=2\alpha.
\]
Since \(X\) lies on the angle bisector at \(B\) and on the altitude from \(C\),
\[
\angle BXC=90^\circ+\frac{\beta}{2}.
\]
Thus
\[
2\alpha=90^\circ+\frac{\beta}{2}
\]
so
\[
\beta=4\alpha-180^\circ.
\]
Then
\[
\gamma=180^\circ-\alpha-\beta=360^\circ-5\alpha.
\]
Acuteness gives
\[
\beta<90^\circ \implies \alpha<67.5^\circ,
\]
and
\[
\gamma<90^\circ \implies \alpha>54^\circ.
\]
So
\[
54^\circ<\alpha<67.5^\circ.
\]
The largest integer value is therefore
\[
\boxed{67}.
\]
